label: vllm
notes: target may use every CPU: llmperfscope shares CPUs with it

load.why: 1.1 CPU cores busy and the GPU 5% busy: host work, spread over threads that take turns.

warmup.why: 0.15 s is too short for the GPU's utilization counter. Use a longer run.

serve_c1.why: GPU clocks were held down by sw_power_cap, sw_thermal at 96% utilization, 2005.0 MHz average.

serve_c4.why: GPU compute is the limit: 98% busy. Use --nsys to see which kernels take the time.

memory.text: GPU memory peaks 324 MiB above its steady level, during load. That peak decides what fits, not the steady level.
The process holds 2.64 GiB of its own host RAM during serve, next to 4.57 GiB on the GPU. If that is a copy of the weights it can usually be released after upload.
The server's cache pool peaked at 6% (vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc). Most of the memory reserved for it was never used at this load; a smaller reservation would fit, unless a heavier load is coming.

serving.text: Going from 1 to 4 concurrent requests raised throughput 3.12 times, and the median first token moved from 21 to 49 ms.

next_steps: --nsys: which kernels take the GPU's time, and what it waits on in the gaps
